def test_clear_keeps_get_records_in_sync(caplog):
    """``caplog.clear()`` must not decouple ``get_records`` from ``records``."""
    caplog.set_level(logging.INFO)

    def verify_consistency() -> None:
        assert caplog.get_records("call") == caplog.records

    verify_consistency()
    logger.warning("test")
    verify_consistency()
    caplog.clear()
    verify_consistency()  # previously failed: get_records still held the old record.
    logger.info("after_clear")
    verify_consistency()  # get_records must keep receiving new records as well.
    assert [r.message for r in caplog.get_records("call")] == ["after_clear"]

Fix caplog.get_records()/caplog.clear() divergence (patch-2, version v4).

Root cause: LogCaptureFixture.clear() called handler.reset(), which reassigned self.records to a new list, while item.stash[caplog_records_key] kept the original list that caplog.get_records() returns — so get_records() froze after clear().

Change:
- src/_pytest/logging.py: added LogCaptureHandler.clear() that clears the existing records list in place and resets the stream; LogCaptureFixture.clear() now delegates to handler.clear().
- testing/logging/test_fixture.py: added test_clear_keeps_get_records_in_sync, the issue's reproduction (asserts get_records("call") == caplog.records before logging, after logging, after caplog.clear(), and after new records are emitted post-clear).

Note on the earlier delivery-1/patch-1: it only added an unused LogCaptureHandler.clear() method and left LogCaptureFixture.clear() calling reset(); it did not change behavior. patch-2 wired the fix in.
